hints: Notice the conditions, hot concentrated NaOH in ethanol favours elimination, not substitution, so think about losing HX to form C=C.
Count what must be lost, J has two Br and one Cl so excess reagent removes 2 HBr plus 1 HCl, and the carbon skeleton plus all methyl groups stay unchanged.
Check each skeleton for the methyl pattern and the total number of double bonds, starting from one C=C plus three new C=C bonds from three eliminations.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Hot concentrated NaOH in ethanol causes dehydrohalogenation of halogenoalkanes. Each C-Br or C-Cl loses HX with a neighbouring H to form a new C=C bond.

$$ \text{R-CH}_2\text{-CHX-R} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-CH=CH-R} + \text{X}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} $$

**Count how many eliminations occur**

Compound J is $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{23}\text{Br}_2\text{Cl}$ and already contains one exocyclic $\text{C=CH}_2$ bond. With excess reagent all three halogens are removed.

$$ \text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{23}\text{Br}_2\text{Cl} - 2\text{HBr} - 1\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{20} $$
So X must have the original C=C plus three new C=C bonds, four C=C bonds in total.

**Keep the carbon skeleton and methyls the same**

Elimination does not break C-C bonds. J is a spiro[5.5] system with two $\text{CH}_3$ groups on the left ring next to the spiro centre and one $\text{CH}_3$ group on the right ring on the C-Cl carbon. X must show the same gem-dimethyl on the left and single methyl on the right.

**Match to the skeletons**

Only the structure with gem-dimethyl on the left, single methyl on the right, the retained $\text{C=CH}_2$ group, and three additional endocyclic double bonds fits all the rules. That is the conjugated diene on the right plus one new alkene on the left.

options.A: Has four C=C bonds which fits the elimination count, but the left ring shows only one methyl instead of the gem-dimethyl of J. Methyl groups cannot be lost in elimination, so this skeleton is impossible.
options.B: Shows the unchanged spiro skeleton with gem-dimethyl on the left, single methyl on the right and retained exocyclic methylene. It has three new endocyclic C=C bonds plus the original exocyclic bond, giving $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{20}$, exactly 2 HBr + 1 HCl removed.
options.C: Shows only one methyl on the left ring, so the gem-dimethyl has been lost, and shows only two endocyclic double bonds plus the exocyclic bond. That is only two new C=C bonds, not three, so one HX elimination is missing.
options.D: Has the correct methyl pattern with gem-dimethyl on the left, but the right ring shows only one endocyclic double bond. Total C=C count is only three, so only two HX molecules appear to have been removed instead of three.
